sources.purpose: Not applied. Pyeongtaek Godeok-dong split into Godeok1/2; jurisdiction adjustment. Legal dong codes unchanged; no national release-unit denominator impact stated.
Jeonnam/Gwangju integrated special city and Incheon code changes. Complete July ZIP and September package independently contain new code names.
Independent official web display verifies Seoul 1100000000 followed by Jongno 1111000000.
Official page separately displays 16 top-level and 227 lower-level governments. Secondary corroboration only; page heading has half-year/June timing, so current-code ZIP remains primary.
Official launch notice states July 1 combination of former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju into Jeonnam Gwangju Integrated Special City.

method.parsing: CP949 fixed-width bytes. code[0:10], sido[11:41], sigungu[42:72], eupmyeondong[73:103]. Legal ri[104:134], created[135:143], abolished[144:152].
method.selection: Among code suffix 00000 rows, include direct city/county/autonomous-district children; exclude top-level province rows, branch offices, and multi-token sigungu names representing general districts. Explicitly include Sejong 3611000000 and Jeju City/Seogwipo. Sort numeric first-five-digit code ascending.
method.counts: 230 = 227 autonomous city/county/district governments + Sejong 1 + Jeju administrative cities 2. 291 source level rows minus 16 top-level rows minus 6 branch rows minus 39 general districts = 230.

caveats: Gyeonggi 31 released status is supplied by parent task context, not independently deployment-verified in this research. Denominator and 31 Gyeonggi unit membership are independently verified from official source.
As-of date controls effective package. Do not apply future 2026-10-12 package on 2026-10-10.

Legal dong and administrative dong are different entities; Jongno has 87 legal dongs, 17 administrative dongs, and 93 official administrative/legal relationship rows. Do not duplicate pages for mapping overlaps.
Ascending official-code order places integrated special city code 12 (27 units) directly after Seoul code 11 and before Busan code 26. Legacy province ordering is obsolete.
Release denominator excludes 39 general districts, including Hwaseong 4; excludes 6 branch offices even when their codes look like district-level codes.
